bounded_results_are_not_proofs: Every 'holds_bounded' above means 'no violating run of at most 10 cycles exists'. Nothing here is an unbounded proof, and no finding claims one.
description: Ground truth for the hal_secprop access-control fixtures, written alongside the generator. The tool must reproduce these verdicts from the netlist and the policy alone.

defects.description: PREADY is driven by a DLH_X1 transparent latch; neither front end models a latch

expected.front_end: raises UnsupportedPrimitives on both the offline and the hal_py path

defects.description: the slot-2 debug write path does not consult the lock, so SECRET can be written while locked
SECRET[3] is a DFFS and comes out of reset as 1 while the policy declares a reset value of 0

secprop/lock-integrity.why: the lock itself is not defective in this variant

witness.why: reset is released at cycle 2, the lock can be engaged by a write at cycle 2 at the earliest, so the first cycle at which a locked debug write can happen is 3. Which cycle >= 3 the solver picks is its own business and is not part of the ground truth.
reset is asserted for cycles 0 and 1 and obligations are instantiated from cycle 1

secprop/lock-integrity.why: the lock bit is set-only until reset

secprop/locked-write-blocked/SECRET.why: both write paths consult the lock, and a write while locked is reachable inside the bound, so the pass is not vacuous

secprop/reset-clears/SECRET.why: every SECRET bit is a DFFR and comes out of reset as 0

structural_claim.statement: the fan-in cones of SECRET in secreg_ok and secreg_faulty are identical -- same inputs, same depths, same external controls, and the lock is in both
structural_claim.why_it_matters: structural reachability cannot distinguish the correct design from the broken one, which is why cone results are reported as candidate paths with status 'heuristic' and never as a verdict
